test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 23 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Some features of transportation in plants are mentioned below. Which option shows the INCORRECT feature?

options.text: Movement of both water and food is bidirectional
Water movement is by simple physical forces; food movement requires energy
Xylem transports water and Phloem transports food
Vessels and Tracheids are dead cells and Sieve tubes are living

solution:
The correct answer is **__Movement of both water and food is bidirectional__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Bidirectional movement means the movement of two molecules in **2 opposite directions.**
 
• A non-living tube called** an xylem transports water **and it runs through the stem from the roots to the leaves. It is** unidirectional **in nature. 
 
• Because sucrose builds up in the **phloem tissue **and absorbs water, causing a high turgor pressure, phloem movement is **bidirectional**. 
 
• Thus, the **movement of water is unidirectional **whereas the movement of **food is bidirectional**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Water movement is by simple physical force, which is **diffusion**, i.e., transport of substances from higher concentration to lower concentration. 
 
• Whereas **food transport is active transport **which requires energy for transport.
 
• Water molecules travel from the soil into the root's living cells and eventually into the **vessels and tracheids**, which serve as the xylem's transport cells. These hollow, dead xylem cells enable quick water movement.
 
• **Sieve tubes **are living cells that are responsible for transporting carbohydrates throughout the plant.
